bifrost: none for app-facing accessory sessions; OS layer: springboard/src/bare/bluetooth.rs (device list, pairing, audio route flag), springboard/src/shell/pages.rs (bluetooth_spec, line 378), springboard/src/bare/input.rs (evdev input devices, shell only), springboard/src/media/v4l2.rs (camera devices, shell only)
summary: Apple's framework connects apps to MFi hardware over Lightning, 30-pin or Bluetooth, with a per-protocol byte stream and connect/disconnect notifications; the doc notes iOS-family apps on Apple silicon Macs cannot use it. BifrOSt has no SDK type for accessory discovery, sessions, protocol matching or Wi-Fi accessory setup. The shell manages Bluetooth pairing and devices, but apps get no API for them.

features.bifrost: none in springboard/sdk/src/ (no accessory module); shell-side device events in springboard/src/bare/bluetooth.rs
features.note: Apps cannot subscribe to accessory attach or detach. The SDK's notification module (springboard/sdk/src/usernotif.rs) is for user notifications, not hardware events.

features.apple: EAAccessory (name, manufacturer, modelNumber, serialNumber, protocolStrings, isConnected, connectionID) https://developer.apple.com/documentation/externalaccessory/eaaccessory
features.bifrost: springboard/src/bare/bluetooth.rs (Device struct: addr, kind, name, paired, connected, audio, rssi)
features.note: The shell has a Bluetooth device record with name, connection and pairing state. It is not exposed to apps and has no MFi protocol strings, manufacturer or connection ID. Wired accessories are not modelled.

features.bifrost: springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs (per-app permission manifest and bubblewrap sandbox)
features.note: No manifest key declares accessory protocols, and the sandbox has no accessory grant. The sandbox binds only /dev/snd and /dev/dri, so an app has no path to a serial or USB device.

features.bifrost: none for apps; springboard/src/term/pty.rs is a pseudo-terminal for the built-in terminal only
features.note: No app-facing byte stream to an accessory. The PTY code serves the terminal app, not hardware.

features.apple: EAAccessoryManager showBluetoothAccessoryPicker (Bluetooth MFi accessory selection sheet)
features.bifrost: springboard/src/shell/pages.rs (bluetooth_spec, line 378, Settings > Bluetooth page); springboard/src/bare/bluetooth.rs (Link/Unlink, pairing)
features.note: The Settings page pairs, connects and unpairs devices, and sets an audio route. No app can open a picker to choose an accessory for itself. The picker is a shell feature only.

features.apple: EAWiFiUnconfiguredAccessoryBrowser, EAWiFiUnconfiguredAccessory, Wireless Accessory Configuration Entitlement https://developer.apple.com/documentation/externalaccessory/eawifiunconfiguredaccessorybrowser
features.note: No scan for unconfigured Wi-Fi accessories and no configuration hand-off. The Wi-Fi stack (netd) is OS-level and has no app API for this.

features.apple: Not in the framework; closest analogue for hardware input is GameController and CoreMIDI (outside this matrix)
features.bifrost: springboard/src/bare/input.rs (evdev discovery, shell only); springboard/src/media/v4l2.rs (V4L2 camera devices, shell only)
features.note: Input and camera devices are opened by the shell. An app that needs a generic accessory cannot get its device path or events through the SDK.

features.apple: Not part of this framework (MFi uses Lightning and 30-pin, which BifrOSt does not expose); USB is covered by AccessoryAccess and serial is not an Apple accessory API
features.bifrost: none in springboard/src/ for USB or serial access by apps (no hits for tty, serialport, hidraw or libusb in SDK code)
features.note: Checked for serial and USB device access in springboard/ with a text search: only the PTY (springboard/src/term/pty.rs), the installer and the DRM driver (springboard/wm/src/drm.rs) matched. Recorded for completeness; the USB side belongs to the AccessoryAccess matrix row.

gaps: No SDK accessory manager or connect/disconnect events for apps (EAAccessoryManager).
No app-facing accessory object with protocol strings, manufacturer, model and connection ID (EAAccessory).
No EASession byte stream for a declared accessory protocol, and no manifest key or sandbox grant for accessory protocols (app_policy.rs binds only /dev/snd and /dev/dri).
No Bluetooth accessory picker callable from an app; the picker exists only in Settings (shell/pages.rs bluetooth_spec).
No Wi-Fi unconfigured accessory browser or configuration flow.
Bluetooth device state (springboard/src/bare/bluetooth.rs Device) is not surfaced through any SDK type.
